core_themes.name: P scales no longer fit for purpose
core_themes.claim: P scales are built on the old national curriculum so do not support progression to the new curriculum, are not moderated, rely on best-fit linear judgements, and have been used as a curriculum, so they should no longer be the statutory assessment.

core_themes.name: Pupils working below test standard are a diverse, disadvantaged group needing different assessment
core_themes.claim: A proportion of pupils have not completed the programmes of study and cannot sit the tests, and they are disproportionately pupils with SEND, disadvantage and EAL, so age-related expectations and mainstream tests do not capture their attainment and progress.

core_themes.name: Non-linear progress of pupils not engaged in subject-specific learning
core_themes.claim: A small number of pupils with severe, profound and multiple learning difficulties will not reach subject-specific learning and progress in uneven, lateral or non-linear ways that linear frameworks such as P scales and pre-key stage standards cannot capture.

core_themes.name: Pre-key stage standards replace P scales for pupils engaged in subject-specific learning
core_themes.claim: Removing statutory P scales and making the secure-fit pre-key stage standards permanent and extended to all pupils in subject-specific learning gives a common language, alignment with the national curriculum and a clear progression route to mainstream assessment.

core_themes.name: Seven areas of engagement for pupils not engaged in subject-specific learning
core_themes.claim: Statutory assessment of pupils not yet in subject-specific learning should focus on cognition and learning through the seven CLDD areas of engagement, which build the prerequisites for subject learning, with schools free to choose their method because progress is individual and non-linear.

core_themes.name: Accountability without national data submission, subject to piloting
core_themes.claim: Schools need not submit seven-areas data to the department and would be held to account through evidence and dialogue with parents, inspectors and others, but because the approach is untested the government will pilot it before deciding whether to adopt it and what data to collect.

proposal.note: The government accepted the pre-key stage standards but deferred the decision on the seven areas model and data collection pending a pilot; no costs or benefits are estimated.

core_themes.name: Phased timetable and pilot
core_themes.claim: P scales are removed and the extended pre-key stage standards introduced from 2018 to 2019, while the seven areas model is piloted in 2017 to 2018 with any change taking effect from 2019 to 2020, so schools have time to prepare and legislation can be amended.

core_themes.name: Reviewing the standards and supporting consistent teacher judgements
core_themes.claim: The interim standards, including the new emerging and entry standards, will be reviewed with experts and consultation feedback, and supported by exemplification materials and a piloted peer-to-peer moderation to make assessments consistent.

core_themes.name: Training, collaboration and guidance for schools
core_themes.claim: Teachers will be supported through ITT and CPD, school-to-school collaboration and sharing of good practice, and updated guidance on assessing pupils with EAL, with the pilot identifying the support schools need.

implementation.note: Implementation detail is largely a timetable and set of support commitments; no costs are given.
